newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank injects T$9 bln in funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank injects T$9 bln in funds.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank on Thursday injected T$9 billion in funds into the banking system through open-market operations to stabilise markets following the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, a bank official said.

The bank, operating through finance companies authorised to issue commercial paper, bought T$9 billion in approved securities instruments offered by financial institutions with yields at between 5.95 and 6.20 percent, the official said.
The institutions have the option of repurchasing the instruments between five and 12 days from now, the official said.
Anaysts said the move was one of the government's measures to stabilise the markets.
Taiwan's stock market gyrated wildly on Thursday on the overnight news of Deng's death, but eventually closed 21.19 points higher, or 0.28 percent, to end at 7678.04.
"The central bank tried to provide enough liquidity to help stabilise the markets, particularly the stock market," said David Yu, vice-president at International Investment Trust Co.
